nodes.description: Mapping address=>uint256 holding token balances; written with unchecked arithmetic in transfer/transferFrom and the constructor.
Nested mapping address=>address=>uint256 of spend approvals; mutated unchecked in transferFrom and set in approve/approveAndCall.
Public uint256 total supply, assigned once in the COREv2Fork constructor.
Public token display name, set in the constructor.
Public uint8 number of decimals, set to 18 in the constructor.
Public token symbol, set to 'COFO' in the constructor.
Public version string initialised to 'H1.0'.
Abstract ERC20 interface declaration returning total supply.
Abstract ERC20 interface declaration returning an account balance.
Abstract ERC20 interface declaration for transfer.
Abstract ERC20 interface declaration for transferFrom.
Abstract ERC20 interface declaration for approve.
Abstract ERC20 interface declaration for allowance.
Transfers _value from msg.sender to _to using unchecked balance arithmetic; intended wrap protection is commented out.
Transfers _value from _from to _to using unchecked balance and allowance arithmetic.
Constant getter returning balances[_owner].
Sets allowed[msg.sender][_spender] = _value and emits Approval.
Constant getter returning allowed[_owner][_spender].
Fallback function that immediately throws on any plain ether transfer.
Constructor that mints the whole supply to msg.sender and sets name/decimals/symbol.
Approves _spender then performs an external call to _spender.receiveApproval - classic external-call-after-state-write pattern.
Caller-controlled address used as mapping key for balances, allowances and token minting.
Unchecked subtraction of _value from balances[msg.sender]; can underflow.
Unchecked addition of _value to balances[_to]; can overflow, especially for address(0).
Unchecked addition to the recipient balance inside transferFrom; can overflow.
Unchecked subtraction from the sender balance inside transferFrom; can underflow (including to address(0)).
Unchecked subtraction from the allowance mapping; can underflow and grant infinite approval.
Low-level external call to attacker-controlled _spender with all gas, executed inside approveAndCall after state is written; reentrancy risk.
Unconditional overwrite of an allowance (approve race condition); no zero-then-set guard.
Constructor mint assigning 10000e18 tokens to msg.sender and totalSupply without overflow check.
Recipient address parameter of StandardToken.transfer.
Amount parameter of StandardToken.transfer, drives unchecked balance arithmetic.
Source address parameter of StandardToken.transferFrom.
Recipient address parameter of StandardToken.transferFrom.
Amount parameter of StandardToken.transferFrom, drives unchecked balance and allowance arithmetic.
Spender address parameter of StandardToken.approve.
Allowance amount parameter of StandardToken.approve.
Attacker-controllable callee address param of approveAndCall; target of the external call.
Approval amount parameter of approveAndCall, forwarded to the external call.
Arbitrary calldata bytes parameter forwarded verbatim to the untrusted external call.

edges.reason: msg.sender indexes the balance that is decremented with unchecked arithmetic.
Transfer amount _value flows directly into the unchecked balance subtraction.
Recipient _to indexes the balance that is incremented with unchecked arithmetic.
Transfer amount _value flows directly into the unchecked balance addition.
msg.sender is checked but its debit enables the credit to _to.
_from indexes the balance decremented without overflow protection in transferFrom.
_value flows into the unchecked subtraction from balances[_from].
_to indexes the balance incremented without overflow protection in transferFrom.
_value flows into the unchecked addition to balances[_to].
msg.sender is the allowance owner whose approval gates the transferFrom credit.
_from is the outer key of the allowance mapping decremented unchecked.
msg.sender is the inner allowance key whose value can underflow to a huge approval.
_value flows directly into the unchecked allowance subtraction.
_spender becomes the inner key of the allowance that is overwritten.
_value is written into the allowance mapping without a zero-reset guard.
msg.sender is the approving owner recorded in the allowance mapping.
Attacker-controlled _spender is the target address of the low-level external call.
_value is passed as an argument into the external receiveApproval call.
_extraData is forwarded verbatim as calldata to the untrusted external call.
msg.sender is passed into the external call, letting the caller spoof _from on reentry.
balances state variable is the storage slot mutated by the unchecked subtraction.
balances state variable is the storage slot mutated by the unchecked addition.
balances state variable is the storage slot mutated by the unchecked transferFrom subtraction.
balances state variable is the storage slot mutated by the unchecked transferFrom addition.
allowed state variable is the storage slot mutated by the unchecked allowance subtraction.
allowed state variable is the storage slot overwritten by approve.
totalSupply is assigned inside the constructor.
StandardToken.transfer executes the unchecked sender balance decrement.
StandardToken.transfer executes the unchecked recipient balance increment.
StandardToken.transferFrom executes the unchecked recipient balance increment.
StandardToken.transferFrom executes the unchecked sender balance decrement.
StandardToken.transferFrom executes the unchecked allowance decrement.
StandardToken.approve unconditionally overwrites the allowance.
The COREv2Fork constructor mints the entire supply with the unchecked assignment.
approveAndCall performs a state-changing approval and then hands control to the untrusted _spender, enabling reentrant calls before effects settle.
Target of the external call can reenter COREv2Fork.approveAndCall or transferFrom/approve to abuse the mutated allowance state.
Fallback throws, so no ether path reaches the minting assignment.

normalization_plan.reason: The transfer recipient parameter is only used as the mapping key of the unchecked balance addition and the Transfer event.
The transfer amount parameter has no independent behaviour; it is consumed solely by the unchecked balance arithmetic.
The source address parameter is a pure index into the balance mapping mutated without overflow checks.
The recipient parameter is only a mapping key for the unchecked credit operation.
The amount parameter drives the unchecked allowance and balance arithmetic and has no other role.
The spender parameter is used only as the key of the allowance overwrite.
The approved amount parameter has no behaviour beyond being stored in the allowance mapping.
The spender parameter is the untrusted call target of the external call, so it merges into that unsafe operation.
The value parameter is passed as an argument into the external receiveApproval call.
The extraData parameter is forwarded verbatim as calldata to the untrusted external call.
